expect: Recognize the reconstruction burden of fragmentary helpers.
An in-place cohesive rendering, preserving the output, is a supported remedy.
Do not require extraction merely to meet function-size preferences.
Retain the one-line key operation when it owns a representation shared by callers.
Do not inline merely because its body is short.
Recognize independent documented policy ownership despite the shared parameterized helper.
Direct, separately owned transformations can remove mode knowledge without introducing layers.
Do not assess whether trimming or quoting is the correct business policy.
Keep the shared canonical representation instead of splitting it by caller name.
Do not expand a duplication assignment into an unrelated wrapper review.
A supported strings.Join replacement can remove custom joining mechanics.
Explain the clearer operation and preserved behavior rather than citing line count alone.
Keep the existing private function boundary or separately justify any removal.
Recognize that CSV encoding is not plain joining and retain its adaptation/error contract.
Do not replace it with strings.Join for brevity; do not invent a correctness audit.
Identify the shared current format-to-media-type decision and both inspected sites.
A small common owner is proportional; do not invent a plugin registry.
Distinguish extension and media-type representations despite matching case labels.
Do not mandate centralization merely to reduce coordinated file count.
Reject correctness-only advice as out of scope rather than accepting it as maintainability.
Do not prescribe empty-input behavior, tests, or a replacement bug-finding pass.
Include review-contract, languages/go, assigned data-flow lens, and finding-template.
Carry exact scope, receipt, revisions, effective policy, and source anchors.
Use a neutral question; do not transmit an expected map-copy finding or peer verdict.
Reject unrelated existing cleanup despite a possibly useful standalone simplification.
Keep the PR boundary explicit; do not turn supporting context into a global backlog.
